# Facts: Hardware, registers and firmware

Register-level behaviour of the GPU and the platform: MMIO, IP blocks, SMU, PSP, interrupts, memory controller, clocks, power and temperature, firmware and BIOS. 107 facts (3 HYPOTHESIS, 72 MEASURED, 30 CONFIRMED, 2 REFUTED).

Source: [`data/hardware.yaml`](data/hardware.yaml). Graphs: [`graphs/hardware.md`](graphs/hardware.md). All areas: [`../facts.md`](../facts.md). Live facts only: [`current.md`](current.md). Links in the text are relative to `docs/` in the data and rewritten for this page.

| <a id="m35"></a>M35 | Loading through the PSP is not passive: the PSP starts what it loads. After the ten `LOAD_IP_FW` and with no other register written by us, `SDMA0/1_F32_CNTL` read 0 instead of 1 (halt released, `SDMA0/1_STATUS2_REG` changes from sweep to sweep), `RLC_CNTL` reads 1 and 31 GC registers hold the value Linux shows after amdgpu's init (RLC power-gating and SERDES state, `CGTS_*_SM_CTRL_REG`, `CC_GC_SHADER_ARRAY_CONFIG_GEN0`, `RLC_SMU_COMMAND = 0x13`: the RLC has talked to the SMU). `CP_ME_CNTL` (`0x15000000`) and `CP_MEC_CNTL` (`0x50000000`) do not change: the CP stays halted until the driver releases it. An unload (`DESTROY_TMR`, ring stop) does not undo this; a warm reboot does.
